impact: Network drives still inaccessible; police reporting, evidence and fingerprinting systems affected
date_note: Date is when the forensic report was made public; the attack itself began in July and encryption launched on 2026-08-16.
title: Fort Smith, Arkansas: forensic report details August ransomware attack on city network
summary: A forensic report by PNG Cyber, made public on 19 November, says intruders were in the City of Fort Smith network from 24 July to 18 August 2026, and that file encryption began on 16 August. Talk Business & Politics reports staff still cannot reach network drives. The threat actor claimed about 5,720 GB of data; Interlock claimed the attack in September.
plain: The city of Fort Smith, Arkansas, was hit by ransomware in August. A new report says attackers were inside for weeks and copied data, and city files are still not fully back.
exec: A months-long municipal outage with data theft shows the cost of long attacker dwell time; 1,032 employees and more than 36,000 account holders may have data at risk.
action: Fort Smith employees and water/sewer customers: use the credit monitoring and identity protection steps the city has announced. Other local governments: review privileged account monitoring.

key_findings: Threat actor access from 2026-07-24 to 2026-08-18; encryption launched 2026-08-16.
PNG Cyber triaged 872 unique city computer systems.
Report records the actor's claim of approximately 5,720 GB of data, comprising 4,882,956 files.
1,032 city employees and more than 36,000 residents and businesses potentially at risk.
recommendations: Use the credit monitoring and identity restoration offered by the city.

validation.note: One publisher (Talk Business & Politics) summarising the PNG Cyber forensic report; the report PDF itself was not opened. The city has publicly confirmed the incident. Interlock attribution is the group's own claim, not a government or investigator attribution.
